clue.text: Anteater finds a way into Bible, with Noah's vessel

indicators.note: into says the abbreviation for a way goes inside the abbreviation for the Bible

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
Noah built the ark in Genesis

explanation.surface: An anteater turns up in the Bible alongside Noah's great boat.
explanation.walkthrough: AV, the Authorised Version, is the standard crossword shorthand for the Bible; 'finds' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The aardvark is an African burrowing mammal that feeds on ants and termites.

clue.text: Animal to fall ill with attack

parts.note: an ass is a donkey, an animal
to ail is to be unwell

explanation.surface: An animal falls sick at the moment it is attacked.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to launch an assault on, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Terrible crises-one is economic downturn

indicators.note: terrible suggests something badly wrecked, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Dreadful crises bring on a slump in the economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' rearranges CRISES plus ONE; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A recession is a period of falling economic activity, a slump.

clue.text: From vehicle, I'll get a standard ice-cream

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
I'll gives its letters without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: An ice-cream van selling a plain cone.
explanation.definitionFit: The plain, default ice-cream flavour is the one made with vanilla pods.

clue.text: One in a couple of runs?

definitions.text: One in a couple of runs?

parts.words: One in a couple of runs?
parts.note: a competitor taking part in a pair of races, while the word itself runs the same both ways

explanation.surface: Someone taking part in a couple of races.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a palindrome: it reads the same in either direction, a couple of ways to run through it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who competes in races is a runner in them.

clue.text: Somewhat crazy, got enclosed in cell

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone a bit mad has been locked up in a cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertilised egg is a single cell, the first stage of an embryo.

clue.text: It keeps some features of Islam out of sight

definitions.text: It keeps some features of Islam out of sight

parts.words: It keeps some features of Islam out of sight
parts.note: features read as facial features: a garment covering the face worn by some Muslim women

explanation.surface: Something hides certain characteristics of a religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'features' suggests aspects of the religion, but means parts of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A yashmak is a veil worn by some Muslim women to cover the lower face.

clue.text: East European river's pronounced smell

indicators.note: pronounced says the river's name is heard spoken, not written

parts.note: the Oder runs along the German-Polish border

explanation.surface: A river in Eastern Europe gives off a strong smell.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour is a scent, especially an unpleasant one.

clue.text: Drawing ten characters on top of cake

indicators.note: characters means the letters of the word ten, here set in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
icing is the sugary layer spread on top of a cake

explanation.surface: Someone sketches the figure ten in icing on a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' treats the word ten as a set of letters to rearrange; 'on top of' fits a down clue, the first piece sitting above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing in the sense of attracting or luring, as an enticing offer does.

clue.text: Can spare defective gland

indicators.note: defective suggests something faulty, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone can do without a faulty gland.
explanation.definitionFit: The pancreas is a large gland that produces insulin and digestive enzymes.

clue.text: Stamp on this slow service, a poor job

definitions.meaning: a cheaper postage stamp buys the slower mail delivery
post in the sense of a job, one of second-rate standing

explanation.surface: Grumbling about a sluggish postal service and a lowly position.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheaper, slower class of mail in Britain, and also a figurative inferior appointment.

clue.text: Almost offend a monarch that's narrow-minded

indicators.note: almost means the word for offend loses its last letter

parts.note: to insult is to offend
R stands for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: Nearly insulting a king who is a bigot.
explanation.definitionFit: Insular describes people cut off from outside ideas, like islanders, hence parochial.

clue.text: Fabric, two-thirds light blue, a little cold

indicators.note: two-thirds means six of the nine letters of the colour name are kept

parts.note: Cambridge blue is the pale blue of Cambridge University

indicators.note: a little means only a small part, the opening letter, of cold

explanation.surface: A fabric that is mostly pale blue with a touch of chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two-thirds' cuts CAMBRIDGE to CAMBRI; 'a little' takes C from cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambric is a fine, dense linen or cotton cloth.

clue.text: Is greed a fault? Dissent

indicators.note: fault suggests something broken or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A moral question about greed, with a call for objection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fault' rearranges ISGREEDA; the 'a' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissent is to hold a different opinion, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Acting family, left-wing and serious

parts.note: red means socialist or left-wing
grave means serious

explanation.surface: A theatrical dynasty known for left-wing politics and solemnity.
explanation.walkthrough: The Redgraves (Michael, Vanessa, Corin, Lynn) are a famous British acting dynasty, known for left-wing activism.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Redgrave and his children formed a celebrated stage and screen dynasty.

clue.text: Holy book found on Ark, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sacred book discovered aboard Noah's ark.
explanation.definitionFit: The Koran is the sacred scripture of Islam.

clue.text: Outlaw used to steal wearing mask

parts.note: to rob is to steal
in means wearing, as in dressed in
a hood covers the head and face like a mask

explanation.surface: A bandit used to steal with his face covered.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood is the legendary outlaw of Sherwood Forest.

clue.text: Splash from son's dish

parts.note: S abbreviates son
a platter is a large serving dish

explanation.surface: Something spills over from the boy's serving plate.
explanation.definitionFit: To splatter is to spatter or splash with liquid.

clue.text: Steal a tiny amount

definitions.meaning: as much as fits between finger and thumb

explanation.surface: Taking a little bit of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a slang verb for petty theft and the noun for a small fingerful.

clue.text: Barged, thus improperly got to front

indicators.note: improperly suggests letters out of their proper order

parts.note: taken as written
to have led is to have gone in front

explanation.surface: Someone shoved their way to the front in an unseemly fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Hustled means pushed or jostled roughly, as when barging through.

clue.text: Render one's account

parts.note: render as giving or depicting, and account as a report: to give a portrayal in words

explanation.surface: Settling one's bill.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests paying a bill (rendering an account), but it means telling the story.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray in words is to give a narrative of something.

clue.text: Clergyman wants Irish back

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman
Erse is the Irish Gaelic language

explanation.surface: A vicar wants the Irish to return.
explanation.definitionFit: Back and reverse both mean the rear side, or to go backwards.

clue.text: Complained about the steak?

parts.note: a slang verb for grumbling formed from the name of the meat of cattle

explanation.surface: A diner grumbled about their meat.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef is slang for to complain, and steak is cut from cattle.

clue.text: One charging a small volume to employer

parts.note: cc is cubic centimetres, a small volume
a user is one who employs something

explanation.surface: A creditor billing a little book to the company boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who brings charges against another is an accuser.

clue.text: About 500 sheets, off-white

parts.note: C is circa, about
a ream of paper is 500 sheets

explanation.surface: Roughly 500 sheets of paper, slightly yellowish.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream is a pale yellowish-white colour.

clue.text: Income in respect of meeting-place

parts.note: re means regarding, in respect of
a venue is where people meet

explanation.surface: Earnings from hiring out a meeting hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is money coming in, takings or earnings.

clue.text: Got up to embrace one girl

indicators.note: to embrace means the word for got up wraps round the numeral

parts.note: rose means got up
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone stood up to hug a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosie is a girl's name.

clue.text: Dukes get no protection when argument gets serious

definitions.meaning: dukes is slang for fists, here bare, without boxing mitts
an idiom for a dispute turning fierce and unrestrained

explanation.surface: Aristocrats are left unguarded once a quarrel turns nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dukes' (fists, from rhyming slang Duke of York = fork, a hand) suggests noblemen.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare fists without mitts, and the idiom for a fight becoming no-holds-barred.

clue.text: Engineers extremely dainty repair

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: extremely means take the extreme letters, first and last, of dainty

explanation.surface: Army engineers make a very delicate fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives DY, the first and last letters of dainty.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy is a cure or way of putting something right.

clue.text: Inflicted capital loss in block transaction

definitions.text: Inflicted capital loss in block transaction

parts.words: Inflicted capital loss in block transaction
parts.note: capital as the head and block as the executioner's block: removal of the head

explanation.surface: A financial loss suffered in a bulk share deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is stock-market talk; capital means head, block the chopping block.
explanation.definitionFit: Executed by decapitation, having the head cut off.
